Spectral Response from a Calibration Lamp

Source: R/response.R
response_calibration.Rd

Measures the relative spectral response of an instrument (the efficiency of the collection optics, fiber, grating and detector at each wavelength) from spectra of a calibration lamp of known spectral irradiance or radiance, such as a deuterium-halogen lamp, with its uncertainty. correct_response() then corrects spectra or line intensities.

Usage

response_calibration(
  lamp,
  reference,
  dark = NULL,
  smooth = 1,
  exclude = NULL,
  segments = TRUE
)

Arguments

lamp

The spectra of the calibration lamp: a numeric vector named by wavelength, or a matrix or data frame with one spectrum per row and the wavelengths as column names (other columns are ignored). Several spectra are averaged.

reference

The certified spectral irradiance (or radiance) of the lamp: a data frame with columns wavelength (nm) and value, and optionally rsd, the relative standard uncertainties of the values (0.03 for 3%).

dark

An optional dark spectrum (or several, averaged) on the same axis as lamp, subtracted from it.

smooth

The width of the smoothing window, in nm. Default is 1; 0 turns the smoothing off.

exclude

Wavelength ranges left out of the response and interpolated: a numeric vector of length 2, a list of them, or a two-column matrix. Default is NULL.

segments

A logical: smooth each detector segment separately (TRUE, default).

Value

An object of class specproc_response, a list with

  • response: a tibble with, for each channel in column order, its wavelength, detector segment, relative response (NA without response), and its relative standard uncertainty rsd, with the parts from the reference (reference_rsd) and from the measurement (measurement_rsd);

  • n_spectra, smooth, exclude and the wavelength range of the reference.

Use correct_response() to correct spectra or line intensities, and plot_response() to draw the response.

Details

The response at each channel is the ratio of the measured lamp spectrum (after subtraction of dark) to the certified irradiance of the lamp, interpolated at the channel. The certified values, often tabulated every few nanometers, are interpolated by a monotone cubic spline of their logarithm; channels outside their range get no response. The ratio is smoothed by a local linear fit over smooth nm, within each detector segment when segments = TRUE (the axis is split where the wavelengths step back or jump, as in wavelength_calibration()), so that the noise of the lamp spectrum is averaged without biasing the steep edges of the response. The channels in the exclude ranges, such as the Balmer lines of a deuterium lamp (486.0 and 656.1 nm) that the certificate leaves out, are interpolated from their neighbors. The response is scaled to a maximum of 1.

The relative standard uncertainty of the response (rsd) combines in quadrature that of the certified values (column rsd of reference, interpolated linearly) and that of the measurement: with several lamp spectra, the standard error of their mean response (each spectrum scaled to a common level first, so that drifts of the lamp output do not count); with one, the noise of the spectrum (estimated from its channel-to-channel differences) averaged over the smoothing window. Certificates often give expanded uncertainties (coverage factor 2): divide them by 2.

The lamp must be measured through the same optical path as the plasma (collection optics, fiber, spectrometer settings), and its spectrum must not be saturated. With a certificate in energy units (W per nm), the corrected intensities are proportional to the spectral radiance (energy units, as units = "energy" of boltzmann()).

See also

correct_response(), plot_response(), line_intensities()

Author

Christian L. Goueguel

Examples

# the certified spectral irradiance of a lamp, every 10 nm, known within
# 3% (simulated here as a blackbody at 3100 K)
planck <- function(wl, t) 1 / (wl^5 * (exp(1.4388e7 / (wl * t)) - 1))
reference <- data.frame(wavelength = seq(250, 850, by = 10))
reference$value <- planck(reference$wavelength, 3100)
reference$rsd <- 0.03

# five spectra of the lamp, through an instrument of unknown response
wl <- seq(260, 840, by = 0.1)
true_response <- exp(-((wl - 500) / 250)^2)
set.seed(1)
lamp <- t(replicate(5, 2e4 * true_response * planck(wl, 3100) / planck(500, 3100) +
                      rnorm(length(wl), sd = 20)))
colnames(lamp) <- wl

response <- response_calibration(lamp, reference)
response
#> Spectral response from 5 lamp spectra (smoothed over 1 nm)
#> 
#> Channels:     5801 (260 to 840 nm, 1 segment)
#> Uncertainty:  median 3% (3% to 12%); reference 3%, measurement 0.038% (medians)
plot_response(response)
